newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania signs trade deals with Slovakia/Czech.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania signs trade deals with Slovakia/Czech.

text.p: Lithuania said on Thursday it had signed free trade agreements with the Czech Republic and Slovakia, paving the way for membership in the Central European Free Trade Association (CEFTA).
"The agreements were signed late Wednesday night," a spokesperson for Lithuanian foreign ministry told Reuters.
She added the agreements will most likely come into effect from January 1 provided they are ratified by the respective parliaments in the autumn.

Lithuania, which quit the former Soviet Union in 1991, is keen on joining CEFTA, an economic grouping of former Communist bloc states comprising Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary and Slovenia.
Czech-Lithuanian trade was worth just over $65 million compared with $54 million in 1994.
Lithuania signed a free agreement with Poland in June and needs similiar pacts with all CEFTA members before it can join the association.
